idea-plugin.name: Lerd
idea-plugin.description:
Manage your Lerd local PHP environment from the IDE. The project you open resolves to exactly one Lerd site, and its logs, PHP version, workers, services, queries and dumps come with it, without a browser tab.

In the status bar

The site's domain and PHP version, greyed out when Lerd is stopped and not drawn at all for a project Lerd does not know. Click it to open the site, restart it, turn HTTPS on or off, pause it, switch PHP version or open the dashboard.

In the tool window

  • Site — domain, framework, branch and path, the PHP and Node version pickers, a toggle per worker and a row per service, laid out in columns that reflow as the window narrows. Services open in the IDE's own Database tool window on this site's database, or as a client shell.
  • Logs — a framework log collapsed into one row per distinct error with how often it happened, and a live tail for PHP-FPM, every worker, every service and nginx. Both are IDE consoles, so a path in a stack trace is one click from the line that threw it.
  • N+1 & Slow — the queries worth fixing, read from real captured traffic rather than from the code, worst first, each linked to the application line it came from and openable as a runnable SQL scratch.
  • Dumps — everything the site captured, split into the lenses the dashboard uses: dumps, queries, jobs, views, mail, cache, events, HTTP, logs, exceptions and messages. Stack traces are read rather than printed, with the first frame outside vendor/ pulled to the top.

Elsewhere in the IDE

The site's containers appear in the Services window with a terminal and a log to follow. The PHP language level, the CLI interpreter and the PHP server entry for Xdebug all follow whatever Lerd serves the site with.

Everything happens over loopback to the Lerd already running as your user. No account, no token, no telemetry, and nothing contacted but your own machine.

Requires Lerd running on the same machine.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.0

First release.

  • Status bar widget with the site's domain, PHP version and quick actions
  • Site, Logs, N+1 & Slow and Dumps in one tool window
  • Containers in the Services window, with a terminal into each
  • PHP language level, CLI interpreter and Xdebug server follow the site
  • Git worktrees resolve to their parent site plus the branch
